argon_final.explanation: The 734.0 s audio recording contains a clean 50 Hz mains hum across harmonics 2, 3, 4, and 6, which exhibit high median signal-to-noise ratios of 193.02, 125.59, 280.63, and 183.63 respectively. Using these harmonics over a 600 s analysis window starting at 0 s yielded a valid frame fraction of 1.0 and a trace standard deviation of 21.25 mHz. Comparing this extracted trace against the 86349 s reference window produced a peak normalised cross-correlation of 0.99967, which substantially exceeds the frozen threshold of 0.87678. The best match stands well above the second-highest peak of 0.78237 by a margin of 0.2173 (z-score 3.33) and places the implied media start at 50769.22 s within the reference window.
argon_final.rationale: The 600 s audio extraction from 0 s using the four high-SNR harmonics [2, 3, 4, 6] (median SNRs 193.02, 125.59, 280.63, and 183.63) achieved a valid frame fraction of 1.0 and a peak NCC of 0.99967, far exceeding the frozen threshold of 0.87678 with a margin of 0.2173 over the second peak of 0.78237. Because the longest calibrated window and cleanest harmonics already provide an unambiguous match at 50769.22 s, no additional configurations are needed.
what_would_change: A claimed recording start time differing from the implied media start of 50769.22 s in the reference window would trigger a material discrepancy review.
An additional passing analysis window whose implied media start disagrees with 50769.22 s would change the status to inconclusive.
Evidence that the 86349 s reference window is from the wrong electrical grid or date range would invalidate the time alignment.
